events.title: Phoenician Maritime Expansion
events.description: Tyre and Sidon send merchant ships across the Mediterranean. King Hiram of Tyre cooperates with Solomon on the temple construction in Jerusalem.

events.title: Egypt's Weak Period
events.description: Egypt is divided and weakened, creating room for Israel's expansion under David and Solomon without threat from the south.

events.title: Assyrian Recovery
events.description: Assyria slowly begins to rebuild its power after a weak period, with new campaigns in northern Mesopotamia.

events.title: Greek Recovery
events.description: The Greek regions slowly begin to recover after the Dark Ages. New settlements, emerging trade, and early forms of polis societies develop.

events.title: Aram-Damascus
events.description: The Aramean kingdom in Damascus grows and becomes an important regional power, sometimes allied with and sometimes at war with Israel.

events.title: Kingdom of Kush
events.description: The Nubian kingdom of Kush rises to power south of Egypt, with its capital first at Napata and later at Meroë.

events.title: Shishak becomes pharaoh
events.description: The Libyan general Sheshonk I establishes the 22nd dynasty in Egypt. He is likely identical to the biblical Shishak who plundered Jerusalem.
